measured.on: the SAP sandbox, through a throwaway report that WAITs p_sec seconds in a temporary package; ten jobs, the report and the package deleted afterwards

schema.EXPECT: where the expected values come from: A4H = measured on the sandbox; 'unmeasured: assumption' = chosen here, with the reasoning in 'assumption'
schema.clock: the injectable clock's start, system time (UTC); every 'at' and offset below is seconds from it
schema.steps: run in order against JOB_OPEN/JOB_SUBMIT/JOB_CLOSE, BP_JOB_READ, SHOW_JOBSTATE, BP_JOB_DELETE and the scheduler
schema.close: JOB_OPEN + JOB_SUBMIT + JOB_CLOSE of job <job>; start/last are offsets for SDLSTRTDT/TM and LASTSTRTDT/TM, period is the PRD* fields
schema.advance: move the clock by <seconds>; the scheduler's timer fires at each due time it passes
schema.tick: move the clock by <seconds> without letting the timer fire first, then one scheduler pass: a start <seconds> late, like the sandbox's tick at hh:mm:51
schema.hostStart: a new scheduler over the same stores, started: what a host start does
schema.runSeconds: how long each instance of the case runs on the clock (an injected report; the sandbox report WAITed)
schema.instances: per job name, the scheduled start of every instance that ran, as offsets, in order
schema.header: the TBTCO fields BP_JOB_READ answers for the job's newest instance
schema.observed: informational: what the sandbox showed that this runtime does not reproduce (not a gate)

cases.title: SDLSTRTDT/TM are system time: a job asked for now+60 waits until exactly then
cases.observed: the sandbox user's time zone was GMTUK (UTC+1 in October); the job started at the system time asked, not an hour off

cases.title: a start in the past is rewritten to the close time and released; a periodic chain counts from the rewritten time
a past start whose latest start has passed too is refused, BT 386, and the job stays P
the successor is made when the instance starts, status S, at the scheduled time + period, not the actual start + period
cases.observed: instance at 224501 started 22:45:51 (the minute tick); its successor's SDLSTRTTM was 224701 and its JOBCOUNT 22455100, made at that start

cases.title: an instance that runs longer than the period skips no instance
cases.observed: the sandbox ran 2 to 3 instances of C at once, bounded by its free background work processes; this runtime has one work process and queues them (ANORMALIES.md)

cases.title: BP_JOB_DELETE of the waiting successor ends the chain
an instance that ends aborted does not stop the chain: its successor already exists
cases.observed: the sandbox aborted a running instance with BP_JOB_ABORT (asynchronous: still R right after, A at the next look, ENDTIME = abort time); the facade has no BP_JOB_ABORT, so here the instance aborts by itself

cases.title: after downtime an overdue released job starts once, and its successor skips to the first future slot of its phase
cases.assumption: not measured: a missed start after scheduler or host downtime cannot be provoked on a shared sandbox. Chosen: a system started after an outage does not replay its missed periodic runs. At host start an overdue released job starts once; its successor goes to the first scheduled time + k * period that lies after the host start, so the chain keeps its phase and stays aligned with the original schedule; the slots in between are skipped. This applies only to a start overdue at host start: while the scheduler is up, an overrun skips nothing (no-skip-on-overrun, measured).

unmeasured: a missed start after downtime (the downtime case is an assumption: start once, skip to the first future slot of the phase)
a latest start time reached while the job waits: here the job is not started and ends A with result EXPIRED; its periodic successor is still made
PRDMONTHS: refused (JOB_CLOSE_FAILED) until calendar-month arithmetic is measured
a periodic start with STRTIMMED = 'X': refused (JOB_CLOSE_FAILED)
a latest start before the start: refused (INVALID_STARTDATE)
